title: Learning by doing, with science at the centre
lead: A full secondary curriculum from JSS1 to SS3, with laboratory work, competitions and practical skills built in.

curriculum.heading: Six years, three national exams
curriculum.text: Students sit BECE at the end of JSS3, and WASSCE and NECO at the end of SS3. JAMB/UTME is the route to university.

stages.name: Junior Secondary
stages.text: Broad foundation in sciences, mathematics, languages and vocational skills. [SAMPLE wording]

stages.name: Senior Secondary
stages.text: Science focus: Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Further Maths and ICT. [CONFIRM subjects]

notes: Teaching is inquiry-based: students ask questions, investigate problems and think critically. Critical thinking is timetabled, so it is explicitly taught.
The science project and workbook programme gives each student a topic. They design an investigation, review the literature, run experiments, analyse findings and defend them before an audience.

Certification Examination, for all learners: a full simulation of WAEC conditions, set and invigilated by Top Tutors, a unit separate from the classroom teachers, so it stays objective. From SS1, every student must pass at least five subjects at 50% or more (English Language, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and one other) before accessing terminal exams, every term from SS1 to SS3. Retakes are allowed until the standard is met.
The best SS2 student each term was registered for the actual WAEC SSCE free of charge, sitting with the SS3 cohort.
Saturday Examination: papers drawn from JAMB UTME past questions on Saturday mornings, followed by practical laboratory sessions. The best performer in each class each term earns a tuition-free term.

labs.heading: Four labs, used every week [SAMPLE frequency]
labs.text: Practical work is part of every science course.

items.name: Chemistry
items.text: Grew from a basic set-up to digital balances, pH meters, burner arrays, distillation units, fume chambers, fire-safety provisions and eyewash stations. Titrations, qualitative and quantitative analysis, reaction-rate and acid-base work. Supports WAEC and NECO practicals.

items.name: Physics
items.text: Optical benches, lenses and prisms, vernier calipers, micrometers, metre bridges, circuits, galvanometers and projectile kits. An electricity and magnetism section and a mechanics zone.

items.name: Biology
items.text: Preserved specimens, charts and models, microscopes and microtomy kits. Food tests, dissection, ecological surveys and osmosis experiments, with environmental science kits and improved storage and sterilisation.

items.name: ICT
items.text: Digital simulations and virtual experiments, computer-based testing (CBT) practice and multimedia tools.

labs.facilitiesNote: Also on campus: a Technical Drawing and Basic Technology studio, commissioned in September 2017, a library and an ICT centre.

fair.heading: Science fair and projects
fair.text: The Annual Science Fair grew from a modest gathering into a festival for students, teachers, parents and guests. It has student-led experiments, yearly themes (Renewable Energy, Digital Technology, Climate Change and Simple Machines) and an Innovation Corner. Department exhibitions in Chemistry, Physics and Biology extend classroom learning.

vocational.heading: Practical skills for life
vocational.text: Started in September 2014, with the first Vocational Day on 12 June 2015. Early departments included Photography, Bead Making, Tailoring, Shoemaking, Knitting, African Cuisine, Pastries, Agriculture, Make-over and Printing. In 2023 they were streamlined to four areas. Graduates have set up their own ventures.
areas: ICT: web design and digital skills, HTML and simple CSS, graphics and online safety
